transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~41 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (SRE, LyraHealth), Marcus Li (Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (CTO)

Summary: Quick root-cause review of the 03/29 latency spike that produced timeouts and some 5xx cascades. Agreed short-term mitigations (throttle + backoff) and a bench+patch to KV-cache to reduce hot-key amplification. Need traces and a follow-up to validate.

Topics: root cause hypothesis (hot key + batching), retry amplification, rate-limiter interaction, KV/prefix cache behavior, short-term throttles, telemetry additions, next steps and owners.

Related links (mentioned): runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pilot-timeouts (note: internal), benchmark spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/bench-lyra (customer link), security pack: https://redwood.docs/security/soc2 (shared).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we'll keep this tight. objective — go over the spike from sunday and what we can do to stop the timeouts and 5xx cascade.
[00:28] Olivia Park: yeah thanks. we saw a big tail — lots of requests hit 1.2s to 3s and then a bunch of retries, some requests ended up with 502s. our frontend reported user impact around 11:12 UTC.
[00:45] Raj Patel: looking at the traces you shared, there's a pattern — a hot path where a few keys get repeated and the prefix KV cache was invalidated because of TTL churn. that caused cold model loads and longer decode times. also noticed batching size spiked during a surge.
[01:12] Marcus Li: when you say "prefix KV cache" — is that the k-v cache for decoder states or something else? the term in our logs was k v cache but might be different.
[01:25] Raj Patel: sorry, yeah sorry k-v cache for KV (key-value) attention cache, it's what we use to avoid re-computing past tokens. if it's thrashing due to hot-keys + short-lived ttl we lose the benefit.
[01:48] Olivia Park: we did rollout a change Friday to reduce TTL for privacy reasons, that could be it. but why did that produce 5xxs — should've been timeouts only?
[02:05] Maya Chen: good q. what tends to happen is the first wave causes longer inferences, frontends retry, retries pile up, hitting rate-limits on the routing layer, then some requests fail fast or hit overloaded pods that return 502/503. retry amplification + rate-limiting leads to a cascade.
[02:33] Priya Singh: so is the primary vector the cache churn or the retry behavior? which one do we fix first?
[02:45] Raj Patel: both but short-term we can reduce amplification by tightening client-side backoff and enforcing a soft throttle at the edge. long term, we want better prefix caching and smarter batching to avoid hotkey amplification.
[03:05] Olivia Park: we do have a global retry policy in the browser layer that retries every 300ms twice — is that too aggressive?
[03:15] Maya Chen: for a backend like this, 300ms is pretty aggressive if backend p95 is 500ms during normal loads. suggest exponential backoff e.g., 200ms -> 500ms and cap at 2 retries for now.
[03:35] Marcus Li: ok we can change that. does Redwood recommend any circuit-breaker or queue limit config on the edge?
[03:44] Raj Patel: yes — our recommended pattern: soft rate-limit per-route (burst 200, steady 50 rps), circuit breaker that opens when 5xx ratio > 5% over 1m, and a queue depth limit on gateway to 1.5s. we can share config snippet.
[04:12] Maya Chen: quick note — this will slightly increase client latencies during a throttle window but prevents full outage. we'll share a config + cost delta doc.
[04:22] Speaker 4: (inaudible)
[04:35] Olivia Park: what about dedicated capacity — would that remove this class of problems?
[04:44] Raj Patel: dedicated helps with isolation and predictable throughput but it doesn't remove hot-key or retry amplification. you still need caching and backoff. dedicated buys headroom; it's a different axis.
[05:05] Marcus Li: we saw some 429s in the logs right before the 502s — I assume those are rate limits. are the 429s coming from Redwood or our gateway?
[05:20] Raj Patel: looks like a mix — some are our global rate-limiter at the edge, some are internal service limits because backend pods got overloaded and returned 429s. that split is important for mitigation.
[05:40] Maya Chen: can you confirm whether the 429s correspond to requests that had the same session key? if yes, then it's hot-spotting.
[05:52] Olivia Park: i'll check. i think many were same customer session ids.
[06:00] Priya Singh: does compression or quantization settings affect latency spikes? econ: we run a q4_0 profile on the pilot.
[06:12] Raj Patel: quantization helps CPU/GPU throughput but doesn't help a KV thrash scenario — it's orthogonal. what's more impactful is batch sizing and routing: if many requests pin to same shard/model instance you get head-of-line blocking.
[06:35] Maya Chen: are you using sticky routing by session?
[06:40] Marcus Li: yes session affinity is on, we thought it would improve cache hits, but maybe it's making hot keys worse.
[06:48] Raj Patel: exactly — sticky routing helps locality but amplifies hot keys; prefer consistent hashing with prefix caching so same logical context hits same cache but requests can spread if overloaded.
[07:10] Olivia Park: what's the easiest quick win?
[07:14] Raj Patel: 1) tighten client retries + exponential backoff 2) add edge soft throttling 3) raise request timeout on the gateway slightly so in-flight decodes have a chance (for example from 1.5s to 2.5s) 4) patch kv-cache TTL to avoid churn (short-term increment TTL for suspect keys).
[07:40] Maya Chen: we can provide change snippets for 1-3, and Raj will run a bench for 4.
[07:50] Speaker 2: there's also a small config on our serving runtime — the continuous batching window opens to 50ms which can increase latency if traffic is bursty, we can reduce to 20ms.
[08:04] Marcus Li: will reducing the batching window increase overall cost?
[08:09] Raj Patel: slightly, because smaller batches are less efficient. but during a spike the p99 is dominated by queueing not token compute, so smaller window reduces tail latency with modest cost impact. we can quantify in the bench.
[08:28] Olivia Park: what telemetry do you need from us?
[08:33] Raj Patel: sampled traces across the spike, request headers (session id), timestamped rate-limiter hits, pod CPU/mem and GPU utilization for the window. X-Request-Id or similar helps stitching.
[08:50] Olivia Park: i'll pull that and share a sample.
[08:55] Maya Chen: thanks. also curious about the autoscaler — there was a mention of delayed scale-up by ~40s.
[09:05] Marcus Li: correct, autoscaler took a while; our k8s cluster had node provisioning delays because of capacity in the region.
[09:16] Raj Patel: that's another reason for rate-limiter and circuit-breakers — cloud provisioning delays are out of our control during pilot. for critical throughput we can discuss dedicated pools.
[09:32] Priya Singh: security question — if we increase telemetry will that impact PII exposure? we have tight compliance needs.
[09:42] Maya Chen: good point. telemetry can be redacted and shared via secure bucket; we support KMS and can sanitize payloads. redwood security pack was shared in the doc links.
[09:58] Olivia Park: we also had a small spike in 5xx with model variant mismatch errors — not sure if that's our routing or model artifact.
[10:07] Raj Patel: sometimes fallback routing to a lighter model variant can cause structured output differences and errors. we'll check which variant was used during the spike. may be a mismatched rollout.
[10:23] Maya Chen: action wise: Raj will spin up a bench with the KV-cache change to simulate hotkey traffic and share results; Maya will send the throttle/backoff snippets and cost delta; Olivia to send traces; Marcus to tweak batching window in a canary.
[10:40] Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
[11:00] Olivia Park: timeline — we want changes in prod-ish pilot by next Thursday if possible.
[11:10] Maya Chen: feasible; bench results may take a couple days. we can do progressive rollouts and monitor.
[11:25] Raj Patel: i'll also instrument a small metric for kvcache-miss-rate and hotkey-concentration and push it to the dashboard. that should give us early warning.
[11:40] Marcus Li: that would be useful. can you set an alert for kvcache-miss-rate > 15% and hotkey concentration > 10%?
[11:50] Raj Patel: yep can do.
[12:00] Olivia Park: ok next — request timeouts. any config to reduce client timeouts while maintaining safety?
[12:10] Maya Chen: increase gateway timeout to 2.5s, and ensure client backoff doubles; also implement retry budget windows to avoid bursts.
[12:22] Priya Singh: retry budget meaning a token bucket for retries?
[12:28] Raj Patel: yes, like a separate retry quota per route, so retries don't swamp primary capacity.
[12:40] Olivia Park: love that.
[12:45] Maya Chen: on documentation — we'll email the runbook with configs and a short checklist for rollout and rollback.
[12:55] Marcus Li: what about load generation — you mentioned 30k requests bench?
[13:02] Raj Patel: correct — we'll run a 30k synthetic at varying qps to reproduce the tail and measure before/after. i'll post the script.
[13:14] Olivia Park: do you have a recommended safe canary percentage?
[13:20] Maya Chen: start with 5-10% of traffic and monitor the kvcache-miss-grade and 5xx rate for 30 min. if stable, ramp to 25% then to 100.
[13:35] Priya Singh: any contractual implications if we ask to increase timeouts or change routing?
[13:42] Maya Chen: not usually for pilot; for production Dedicated we would discuss SLOs and SLAs. we can align with your security/compliance constraints.
[14:00] Olivia Park: side question on logs retention — we may need longer retention to analyze. what's the cost?
[14:08] Maya Chen: we can share pricing; larger retention has marginal cost on storage but useful during incidents. i'll include numbers in the email.
[14:20] Marcus Li: are there any quick config we can change today to reduce noise?
[14:27] Raj Patel: flip client retry to exponential with cap, and put soft throttle on edge. both are small config changes.
[14:40] Olivia Park: we'll patch client tomorrow.
[14:46] Maya Chen: perfect. final recap and owners in the notes.
[14:55] Raj Patel: running bench and telemetry additions, sharing scripts.
[15:05] Olivia Park: i'll share traces and enable extra telemetry.
[15:12] Maya Chen: i'll email throttle config and cost delta, include SOC2 notes.
[15:20] Priya Singh: thanks all.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
